title: Max Consecutive Ones II
statement: You are given a binary array `nums` (every entry is `0` or `1`). You may change at most one `0` into a `1`. Return the length of the longest run of consecutive `1`s the array can contain after that change. Changing nothing is allowed, so an array of all `1`s simply returns its length.
notes:
## Intuition

The brute force flips each `0` in turn and measures the longest run of `1`s, which is O(n²). Flipping one zero is the same as asking for the longest stretch of the array that contains **at most one** `0`. That is a classic variable-size window: grow it on the right, and shrink it from the left only when it holds a second zero.

## Approach

1. Keep a window `[left, right]` and count the zeros inside it in `zeros`.
2. Move `right` across the array; when `nums[right]` is `0`, add one to `zeros`.
3. While `zeros > 1`, slide `left` forward, subtracting one whenever the element leaving the window is a `0`.
4. The window now holds at most one zero, so flipping it gives `right - left + 1` ones; keep the largest in `best`.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 0, 1, 1, 0]`. For `right = 0..3` the window `[0, right]` holds one zero at most, so `best` grows to `4` (the window `[1, 0, 1, 1]`). At `right = 4` a second zero arrives and `zeros = 2`; `left` moves past index 1 (the first zero) and stops at `2`, so the window is `[1, 1, 0]` of length 3. The answer stays `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): `right` and `left` each move forward at most n times.
- Space: O(1): only three counters, so the idea also works on a stream if you remember the index of the last zero instead of rereading `nums[left]`.

## Pitfalls

- An array with no zeros must return its full length; the window never shrinks, so this falls out naturally.
- An array of only zeros still returns `1`: one zero can be flipped.
- Decrement `zeros` only when the element leaving the window is a `0`, not on every step of `left`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `left` | first index of the current window |
| `right` | last index of the current window |
| `zeros` | number of `0`s inside the window |
| `best` | longest valid window seen so far |

narration.3: No zeros are inside the window yet.
narration.4: The longest window found so far.
narration.6: Extend the window one element to the right each step.
narration.7: Is the new element a zero?
narration.8: Yes: the window now holds one more zero.
narration.10: Two zeros cannot both be flipped, so shrink the window until only one remains.
narration.11: Is the element leaving on the left a zero?
narration.12: Then the window loses that zero.
narration.14: Move the left edge one step right.
narration.16: The window has at most one zero, so its whole length can be ones; keep the best.
narration.18: Return the longest run achievable with one flip.
